items.title: Final Fantasy 14 Players Deliver Perfect Response to 2026’s PHP Vulnerability
items.summary: Warriors of Light across the world proved, once again, why the MMO's community is special
items.content:
By Willa Rowe Published Oct 24, 2026, 5:05 AM EDT Willa Rowe is a contributing writer at Polygon, covering games and entertainment. She is a New York-based journalist and critic whose work has been featured in Kotaku, Digital Trends, the A.V. Club, GamesRadar+, and more. She also co-hosts the Girl Mode podcast. News Warriors of Light across the world proved, once again, why the MMO's community is special

Add Polygon.com on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover Sign in to your Polygon.com account Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread 2 Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap A number of major websites and services went offline earlier this week thanks to a massive PHP security vulnerability . One such service was Final Fantasy 14 . That posed a major problem for plants. You see, Square Enix's MMO has a number of systems on real-world timers that continue regardless of whether a player is logged in. Those unlucky enough to be locked out of the game during the PHP issue were left fearing that their gardens would wither and die. Thankfully, the community stepped in.

Final Fantasy 14 did not shut down completely across the globe, meaning some players were still able to wander Eorzea. These players took it upon themselves to lend a helping hand. One such player made a post on Reddit (spotted by PC Gamer ) that simply offered " PHP Watering Service ." It was exactly what it sounded like. The player invited others to reply or DM with the location of their in-game home so they could, at no cost, water plants for those in need.

Image: Square Enix via Polygon Other players had similar ideas, with more watering service posts popping up on X . Mechanically, this is all possible because of a neat feature of the MMO. There is no special requirement for watering plants, and players can water any plant in the game, even those in other players' homes. This created a communal aid network across the internet that allowed everyone's plants to stay hydrated and healthy. It's just one example of how Warriors of Light are willing to help each other out in the most unexpected ways. There is a reason why Final Fantasy 14 's community has such a good reputation.

After roughly 24 hours of frantic work on the PHP issue, Square Enix has started allowing new logins . That means players should be able to get back to Eorzea and begin taking care of their plants themselves. As the PHP security vulnerability only lasted about one day, nobody's plants should have died.

While the game being back online is a good thing, it does come with one caveat. Square Enix briefly paused housing auto-demolition, which reclaims inactive housing plots if the owner fails to access the building within a certain time limit. That system exists because Final Fantasy 14 's housing is not instanced, meaning there is only a finite number of plots per server. Now that the PHP issues are solved, auto-demolition will resume on Oct. 26.

Websites and services ranging from 4Chan to Spotify are all at risk

items.title: How a data centre united Australia's gaming community
items.source: ABC News & Headlines – Australian Broadcasting Corporation
items.summary: After years of playing on distant worlds, Australian gamers of the popular Japanese role-playing game Final Fantasy XIV discovered a new home. Now that community has welcomed the game developers Down Under.
items.content:
Michael-Christopher Koji Fox (left) and Toshio Murouchi (right) were the main attractions for players at PAX Australia. ( Supplied: Square Enix )

Link copied Share Share article Before the Oceania data centre arrived, Australians sometimes found the online role-playing game Final Fantasy XIV a surprisingly lonely multiplayer experience.

On the Asia server, they'd struggle to find enough fellow English speakers to tackle the game's notorious super-bosses. Those visiting American servers would find the in-game Golden Saucer amusement park sparsely populated during another time zone's twilight hours.

And the few who chose the most distant Europe server struggled with "input lag" that perilously delayed gameplay actions, with the risk of failed quests and let-down teammates.

That changed in January 2022, 12 years after the game was released, when, encouraged by a pandemic boom in player numbers, developer Square Enix finally launched Oceania servers. It was a decision that united players in the region.

Lin, a Final Fantasy XIV community organiser from Melbourne, was shocked at the scale of the local player base.

"When they finally released a server where our ping [internet connection latency speed] was manageable, we were like, 'whoa, there's thousands of people here'," they tell ABC Arts.

"It took 30 minutes just to get into the queue. You no longer had to guess if we could speak the same language or understand the same lingo."

Final Fantasy's near-40-year legacy lured Pat, another community organiser from Melbourne, into online role-playing games.

"I love the Final Fantasy series. That's the one I grew up with," they say.

The Final Fantasy series has nabbed more than 212 million sales. ( Supplied: Square Enix )

By nature, Final Fantasy XIV's community primarily exists online. A community organisation called Limsa Extreme runs in-game award shows, theatre shows and musical productions throughout the year.

Local bar meet-ups are an infrequent occasion, but the annual Final Fantasy XIV community meet-up at PAX Australia, one of the country's biggest exhibitions of games and gaming culture, is the highlight on the calendar.

"The community is so tight-knit when they come together; but it's coming together, that's the hard part," Pat says.

items.title: Final Fantasy XIV re-opens PC logins after players form a ‘PHP Watering Service’ to keep crops alive
Final Fantasy XIV players are helping each other water their gardens during the game’s security incident
items.summary: The past few hours have been quite difficult for Final Fantasy XIV players. After being affected by a serious PHP security vulnerability, the MMORPG had…
items.content:
The past few hours have been quite difficult for Final Fantasy XIV players. After being affected by a serious PHP security vulnerability, the MMORPG had to undergo emergency maintenance and suspend PC connections. Thus, the community went on to help each other out to complete a very specific task.

Players affected by this maintenance faced a problem: they could no longer log in to water their in-game gardens. If crops aren’t watered frequently, they can die. To address this, an initiative called the Player Helping Player Watering Service was launched.

On forums like Reddit, those users who still had access to the game offered to water the gardens of players who couldn’t log in. Players began sharing the coordinates of their homes in Final Fantasy XIV online so that their crops could be saved. Since watering indoor plants requires special permission, these indoor gardens will unfortunately be lost.

Regardless, this initiative is still commendable and demonstrates the spirit of mutual aid that a gaming community can show.

items.title: Final Fantasy 14, Umamusume: Pretty Derby, and more impacted as PHP vulnerability outages hit games around the globe
items.summary: If left unaddressed, the PHP vulnerability may have resulted in serious security issues for games including Final Fantasy 14 and Umamusume: Pretty Derby.
items.content:
Image credit: Eurogamer / Square Enix News by Connor Makar Reporter Published on Oct. 22, 2026, 2:11 p.m. 24 comments Follow Final Fantasy XIV: Shadowbringers Prioritise us on Google Multiple games - including Final Fantasy 14 and Umamusume: Pretty Derby - have faced outages and other issues following this week's discovery of a serious PHP vulnerability.

This vulnerability could potentially result in substantial security breaches for the massive number of websites and applications built using the PHP programming language. As a result, it was advised that online services built upon it should be taken offline until a fix could be distributed and applied. Inevitably, games were caught up.

An official post made to the Final Fantasy 14 lodestone website informed users that security "enhancements" were being made to the MMO's patch servers. As a result, new logins were temporarily disabled until the updates could be completed. While logins have since been turned back on , the server back-up feature for user's save data remains offline.

Horse racing gacha game Umamusume: Pretty Derby, meanwhile, was taken offline completely . As its server-side infrastructure uses PHP, a sudden maintenance outage was put in place - though its developer assured players no exploitation of the security vulnerability had occurred. Right now, Japanese and global servers are back online, with a compensatory package of in-game currency being sent to all players.

Path of Titans, an in-beta dinosaur MMO (which sounds awesome by the way) is still down as of writing. In an announcement made to its official X account , developer Alderon Games explained the MMOand its website had been taken down for up to three days as a precautionary measure. Players were also assured no data had been compromised.

One hopes the chaos is largely over now a fix is in circulation. But even if it is, the fact that so many services all across the globe - far beyond the games industry - have rushed to protect the sanctity of their data and that of their users speaks to the seriousness of the situation. Take a moment to thank the tech heads out there who may have had to work around the clock to get this sorted.

items.title: Wisdom of Nym: Looking ahead to the next few months of Final Fantasy XIV’s waiting game
Everything We Know About Final Fantasy 14 Evercold So Far
items.summary: 8.0 is shaping up to be the biggest revamp of the MMORPG since A Realm Reborn
items.content:
We’re a little less than a month away from Final Fantasy XIV Fan Fest Tokyo which will likely contain some of the final major bits of info we’ll get on Evercold ahead of its January 2027 release. But even now, there’s still a lot we know about the expansion which is looking like the most significant update to the game and its systems since Creative Studio III literally blew up the world with A Realm Reborn 13 years ago. Here’s what we know.

Evercold will come with two new job classes and we’ve already seen the first—bastion. The bastion is a tank class wielding its signature weapon, the skyltborg. What’s that you ask? Imagine a gunblade, now make it a gunshield…that also has a blade. In the class’s brief overview trailer, you can see the skyltborg defend with giant shields, attack at range with bursts of aether fire, while also getting into melee range to dice shit up. It’s an unholy amalgamation of three different disciplines—melee dps, ranged dps, and tanking—that somehow manages to work. We haven’t had official confirmation of the second class, but we know it will feature ranged physical damage. Fan theories suggest the class involves a crossbow and PC Gamer has a neat breakdown that makes a strong case in support of that.

Perhaps the biggest draw to Final Fantasy XIV , beyond the at times legendary storytelling, is the incredible detail with which players can customize their avatar. With Evercold , the game is getting a wealth of new customization options including changing Au Ra horns, nose shadings, face paint, and custom color picking for eyes, hair, and skin tones. Additionally, customization options are also coming to animations giving players the ability to have unique looks for their teleport spell and other class-specific actions.

Evercold is really taking the theme of customization to heart because for the first time, players will be able to choose how they progress in the main story quest. Where in previous expansions unfolded linearly, Evercold will allow players to choose where they take the story next, and conversations with NPCs will reflect the choices they’ve made. In the example shared by Square Enix, a player finishes area A and has the choice of visit areas B, C, or D in any order. To make sure everything progresses smoothly no matter which choice players make, each area will automatically balance its content commensurate with player levels.

One of the biggest complaints about FFXIV of late his how samey all the classes feel. All tank, melee DPS, ranged DPS, and healer abilities feel like palette / flavor text swaps of the same four-five basic actions. It seems Square Enix have heard these gripes, revealing the new “evolved” combat system for Evercold which seeks to return a sense of individuality to the job classes by streamlining their abilities (which, in turn, helps out newer players by cutting down all the buttons and ability rotations they have to learn.) Square Enix hasn’t shared the “evolved” forms of every class yet, but there are a few out there with breakdowns of how the new abilities and combos will work. But if you’ve grown too used to the way things have always been done, FFXIV will keep the old ways in place with “reborn” mode.

Evercold will also rearrange how players spend their time to cut down on the massive grind as players level multiple job classes at the level cap. Currently, to keep up with the choco-bonses you have to complete daily quests to amass the currency you use to buy higher level gear. That system will go away in favor of a weekly system in which you choose quests you can complete on your own time that’ll award you activity points…used to buy higher level gear.

Another time sink is acquiring high level gear across multiple classes. It is tough when you play more than one job class, as each one requires a different set of gear and you gotta work for all that shit. Evercold attempts to cut through that never-ending hamster wheel by allowing players to “reflect” their gear with the highest item level (essentially the highest tier of gear you own) to their other max-level job classes. It won’t work for further gear enhancements like materia, so you still gotta work for your best-in-slot stuff, but it should still make it easier to bring your second and third job classes up to speed.

Your chocobo companion is your trusty steed. You do everything together with one big caveat, you can’t take them into dungeons with you. Evercold will change that, updating the companion system to allow chocobos as combat party members. This means, if you really hate waiting in the duty finder queue, you can run a dungeon with just one other person, your two chocobos taking up the final two slots.

items.title: Final Fantasy XIV Diesel Apparel and Merchandise Revealed
items.summary: Italian brand Diesel has released a new Final Fantasy XIV-themed collection of apparel and merchandise in Japan.
items.content:
A new merchandise lineup based on Square Enix’s Final Fantasy XIV has appeared courtesy of the Italian brand Diesel. The latter revealed it via its Japanese official website and social media account .

The premium brand sells a variety of items ranging from apparel to necklaces and phone cases. However, all of them cost more than ¥10,000. The most affordable ones are moulded cases for the regular and Pro versions of iPhone 17, both of which have the same price tag of ¥11,000 (~$69.80). Meanwhile, the most expensive item in this lineup is the FF-D-Barus Jacket , which costs a whopping ¥132,000 (~$837.85).

The median price of this collection is ¥23,100 (~$146.50), which falls on the T-Norm shirts with ten different back designs available. These designs are also available to view right below:

This collaboration adds yet another entry to the list of merchandise collections based on Final Fantasy XIV . In August 2026, Square Enix released the Emet Selch Earring and perfumes inspired by 21 in-game jobs. It also worked with its subsidiary Taito to bring back the Mini Lamp Quest icon magnets as arcade prizes, as well as Suntory to sell cans with sticker labels featuring the MMORPG’s characters via vending machines.

The Diesel x Final Fantasy XIV Capsule Collection merchandise is now available in Japan. The items are based on the MMORPG readily accessible worldwide on PC, PlayStation 5, PlayStation 4, Xbox Series X, and Switch 2 .

items.title: 24-Year-Old Final Fantasy MMORPG Finally Gets A Generous Free Trial
items.summary: Those looking to jump into Final Fantasy XI can now access the entire base game without time restrictions
items.content:
Final Fantasy XI Final Fantasy XIV Square Enix

Final Fantasy XI rarely gets any updates these days, but fans still have a ton of love for Square Enix’s first attempt at turning its hit RPG franchise into an online behemoth. Now the game that began life on the PlayStation 2 is getting a more generous free trial nearly a quarter century later.

The 2002 release of Final Fantasy XI aimed to exploit the then-booming MMO craze alongside hits like World of Warcraft . Final Fantasy XIV , while not quite as popular today as it was at its peak, has enjoyed ongoing success which has helped revitalize interest in Square Enix’s first MMORPG. The 2002 game is certainly dated by modern standards, but newcomers now have a fresh reason to experience its old-fashioned gameplay sensibilities thanks to a revamped free trial that ditches time limits and raises the level cap to 75.

The game was first released as an online-only PS2 MMORPG before being ported to PC months later, with an Xbox 360 version eventually being released in 2006. Services for both console versions endured until 2016. Since the game’s initial release, there have been no fewer than five expansion packs and eight additional scenarios, with the latest released just a few years ago. The game even saw a boost in players in 2025 thanks to new quests in Final Fantasy XIV that tied back into the narrative of the original game.

But though long-time fans continued to trudge along with the game, the free trial was so stingy compared to the one offered by FFXIV that players would often meme about the discrepancy. Unlike the high level cap with no time restrictions and free access to story content across multiple expansions offered for XIV , the free trial for XI previously only allowed players to level a single character to 50, with a time limit of just 14 days before a paid subscription was needed. Both requirements have now been relaxed .

Not everything is open to free players. The free trial still limits you to the base game content only, and your account can’t hold more than 100,000 gil (in-game currency) at any one time. You’re also not allowed to trade or use the in-game auction house to acquire equipment and items. While you can join a party of other players, you can’t create one.

Personally, I just find it impressive that a PS2-era MMO like Final Fantasy XI is still able to find an audience. Changes like these can only help the game to continue finding success, perhaps for another 20 or more years. Maybe.

items.title: Review: Final Fantasy XIV on Nintendo Switch 2 is the best version of the game
items.content:
I have wanted to get back into Final Fantasy XIV for quite some time. I am a massive fan of everything it offers, from the art direction to the scope of the world and adventures that are held within it. I love the way that it handles narrative within the MMO format, and the massive range of locations to visit. I really, really love the music (I went to a FFXIV symphony and everything), and just generally the very Final Fantasy design of it.

Related reading: To think that I played this for the first time way back on the PlayStation 3. My thoughts back then.

But – and it’s a big but – Final Fantasy XIV is a MMO, and MMOs do demand a time commitment, both in terms of the raw hours you plug into it, and the frequency with which you need to play. Take a big break from an MMO, and it just becomes progressively more difficult to step back into.

I tried to get back into FFXIV once when I first picked up the ROG Xbox Ally . The device handled the game just lovely, but I’m not a frequent PC player, and so at some point I put the device down, took a long break, and just… let my subscription slip again.

I am, however, a frequent Nintendo Switch 2 player. By that I mean “daily”. And so now, with the game’s little icon sitting right there on my Switch 2 home screen, I’ve been logging in for at least a little playtime every day. I’ve already made significantly more progress than I did on the ROG.

Final Fantasy XIV plays just lovely on Switch 2, to start with that important point. The console’s screen is just large enough to be able to handle the very busy interface (it’s an MMO, it’s necessary) without distracting from the core action when you want to watch the fireworks. The game’s visual engine is just now ever-so-slightly showing its age with relatively primitive character models and textures – it has been going for something like 13 years at this point – but the art direction is still as stunning as ever, and I’ve loved revisiting my favourite parts of the world from my first playthrough.

Speaking of, I have started a totally fresh character and save file (I wouldn’t even be able to track down my original avatar from a decade ago, if she still exists on servers somewhere, even if I wanted to. I can’t remember my username, password, or the email address it was attached to). I love how it’s possible to play through all the base game and early expansions with NPCs, and not rely on parties of humans for the various dungeons. If you’ve ever played a FFXIV dungeon before, you’ll know that human allies tend to… well, race through it. One of the few unpleasant memories I have from my first playthrough of Final Fantasy XIV was getting to the very final dungeon of the base game and basically missing the whole thing (and being left behind) because I was trying to follow the story. The conclusion to literally dozens of hours of play.

Now, thanks to NPCs, you can enjoy most of the many expansions and all the stories within them at your own pace. And enjoy the typically excellent music, enemy layouts and dungeon design without feeling rushed, too. I even took time to take screenshots, which is one of my favourite ways to log my adventures in this game.

There is a downside, though. Because Square Enix wants to funnel players into the later expansions where, from their perspective, all the value to the players is, they’ve taken steps to streamline the earlier parts of the game, meaning that you accumulate experience points much (much) faster, and have to do far (far) fewer quests along the way. I have been exclusively undertaking the main quest line, with no side quests, let alone grinding, and my avatar is more than twice the minimum recommended level for any given quest or boss battle.

I understand why they did this, because otherwise it would be a truly intimidating, overwhelming task for a completely new player to get up to the newer expansions, but it means that those same players don’t get to spend enough time in parts of the world to really enjoy their contribution to the whole. The major cities are fine, but you’ll fly through little town areas where previously you’d spend a gaming session or two completing all the side quests. They’re barely blips and blink-and-you’ll-miss-them moments now, which really messes with the pacing for what was previously a truly wonderfully paced game that slowly walked you from one wonder to the next.

I don’t necessarily know what the solution is there, though if it were possible, I would have appreciated the option to toggle whether I wanted the accelerating levelling on or not.

Still, that’s my only gripe. The only other minor issue is that, when it comes to the chat, the Switch’s virtual keyboard doesn’t exactly allow for the same typing speed as a proper keyboard. I don’t even know if it’s possible to connect a Bluetooth keyboard to the Switch 2, as I haven’t tried yet, but even if it were possible, that would significantly undermine the portability of the experience. Currently I haven’t been social enough in FFXIV to require the chat function much, but I can see that becoming an issue later on in the game.

Those are only minor quibbles, obviously, set against a game that is hundreds upon hundreds of hours in scope, and now in an extremely portable and accessible format. FFXIV is a hobby all by itself, and now I can embrace and indulge it in full.
